subject: VectorHealth private listing: SLA & activation plan
messages:

Cc: procurement@vectorhealth.com, alicia.wong@vectorhealth.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private listing / SLA questions and procurement next steps

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the call today — VectorHealth is interested in moving forward with the Azure private listing, but procurement/legal want to confirm a few items before we can issue a PO:

- Can you provide the most recent SOC2 attestation and the Data Processing Addendum (DPA)? Our security team needs the SOC2 PDF and the DPA signed or redlined.
- We need a proposed SLA with uptime% and credit language; procurement typically pushes for a 99.95% target with financial credits. Can Redwood share a draft SLA and highlight any non-negotiable clauses?
- For billing: PO vs invoice cadence (Net30 vs Net45). Procurement prefers Net45 for new vendors; will Redwood accept Net45 for an initial 12-month commitment?
- Activation plan: we need an ETA for when the private listing can be activated in our tenant and the co-sell routing setup. We’d like a mutual action plan with milestones so our internal PM can track.

I’ve attached a first-pass SOW and a short internal checklist (VectorHealth_SOW_v1.pdf). I’ll loop in procurement and legal on this thread.

Can you confirm what you need from our side and an estimated timeline?

Best,
Daniel Ruiz
Head of IT Procurement
VectorHealth

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Short answers and proposed next steps below.

1) SOC2 / DPA: attaching our SOC2 attestation and a standard DPA. If procurement needs specific redlines, Ben is on copy and can take that through legal.
2) SLA: attaching Redwood_SLA_draft.docx — it reflects our standard marketplace SLA (99.9% target with tiered credits). Ben, can you summarize the key negotiation items?
3) Billing: we can accept Net45 for the initial 12-month commitment; commercial will need a signed PO + the DocuSign envelope.
4) Activation & co-sell routing: suggested mutual action plan below (2-week activation):
   - Day 0: Sign DPA + PO / DocuSign
   - Day 2-5: Redwood ops enables listing and seller authorization in Azure tenant
   - Day 6-9: Co-sell routing verification with Azure + test transactions (canary traffic)
   - Day 10-14: Full activation and handoff to VectorHealth CS
We can offer a small onboarding credit (2,000 API units) to use during the canary window. Marissa will confirm credit and commercials.

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_draft.docx, DataProcessingAddendum.docx, SOC2_2025_attestation.pdf

Would you be available for a short sync tomorrow to walk the plan and agree on PO wording? 10am PT works for us.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Partner Success, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private listing / SLA questions and procurement next steps

Daniel — polite/legal review below. High level: most of VectorHealth's asks are reasonable; a few points will need limited compromise.

Key items:
- SLA uptime & credits: Redwood is generally comfortable with a 99.9% target. Financial credit language is acceptable in principle but we need a cap (our standard is cumulative credits capped at 12 months of fees).
- Indemnity: VectorHealth requested broad indemnity and no-fault termination. We can accept breach-based indemnity with liability limited to fees paid in prior 12 months.
- Data residency / audit rights: we will provide SOC2 and support reasonable audit requests but will limit frequency and require redaction for multi-tenant infrastructure details.
- Termination for convenience: we prefer 60 days' notice rather than immediate termination; we can discuss for enterprise addenda.
- PO / payment terms: Net45 is fine for the first year.
I attached a redline of the SLA and a short DPA edit (Redwood_SLA_redline.docx). If VectorHealth legal can accept the redline, we can route the final to DocuSign. If there are any non-starters, flag them and we’ll escalate to the General Counsel.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Daniel — quick commercial notes from my side:

- Onboarding credit: confirmed — we’ll allocate 2,000 API units as a one-time onboarding credit applied during the canary window.
- Pricing: the quote in the SOW stands; I can prepare an amendment reflecting Net45 payment terms and the credit.
- Co-sell routing and seller authorization: Grace’s ops plan looks good. I will open an Azure seller authorization request today; it typically takes 48–72 hours once Azure accepts the MPN linkage. Please confirm which VectorHealth tenant ID we should use (send to me off-thread if needed).
- Go/no-go call: 2027-06-03 10:00am PT works for our ops and sales engineering. Agenda: PO timing, DocuSign envelope, SLA redline walk, and canary plan.

Thanks — we’ll have the DocuSign envelope ready pending your legal sign-off.
